contract.sync_assumed: the whole hardware warp calls the primitive together (all logical warps at once), as the harness does
contract.sync_performed: shuffles, ballots and one any-vote over the full hardware warp, no barrier
contract.type_constraints: bf16 keys only, one row of N keys per logical warp of 8 or 16 lanes packed as bf16x2 words (even items set A in the low halves, odd items set B in the high halves), one more bitonic merge on one-key words after the SIMD network, int32 source indices derived from the position. fp32 unsupported
contract.nan_behavior: a NaN key is never selected (it loses every max.bf16x2 and min.bf16x2 against a number and both set.gt and set.eq are false), so with fewer than k non-NaN keys output slots stay unwritten. Focus-set inputs carry no NaN. -0.0 equals +0.0: the network orders -0.0 below +0.0, the recovery classifies by IEEE comparison, the selected set is the oracle's set in every case (signed_zero pattern passes under both requirements). Denormals compared as values
contract.tie_break_support: both unsorted requirements with the same code: the tie class at the k-th key fills the remaining slots, in index order whenever it has to be capped (prefer_smaller_index exact by construction), measured identical throughput under both requirements in every cell
contract.sorted_output_support: none: the greater class is written in lane order, then the tie class (lane order on the common path, index order on the capped path). A sorted output would need one shuffle per selected key to move the recovered index to its network position
contract.k_range: [1, N / 2] with MaxK = round_up(k, LW) dividing N / 2, measured k 4, 16, 32, 64
contract.n_range: N = 2 x LW x words with (N / 2) / MaxK a power of two, measured N 32, 64, 128 at LW 8 and 16

correctness.notes: Oracle battery (13 cases) passed on every cell under both requirements. Control W1_eager_same_sub in the same lock section, final commit 8f613a317f (batch b3). prefer_smaller_index and not_guaranteed share the common path but compile to different kernels in the fast form (the exact ballot fallback is compiled in for prefer_smaller_index, the capped prefix for not_guaranteed), and the prefer_smaller_index kernel carries 3 to 16 more registers and runs 2 to 4 percent slower in throughput in most cells (up to 9 percent at LW 8 N 128), a T28 schedule and register effect of code that never executes on random input. The exact form compiles the same code for both requirements and measured identical throughput to 0.1 percent.

low_level: Throughput kernels (ternary exchange form, both recovery paths compiled, BRA.DIV duplicated body as in every sub-warp kernel of the harness): 440 to 1752 SASS instructions at LW 16, 560 to 2856 at LW 8, registers 32 at N 32 (8 blocks per SM), 38 to 48 at N 64 (5 to 6), 40 to 60 at N 128 (4 to 6).

The one-word final merge at LW 16 has 4 stages (MaxK 16) and at LW 8 three (MaxK 8) on half-empty words, plus one mirror shuffle per tile word, a smaller share of the call than at warp scope (5 stages of 75).
algorithmic: Same-session throughput against W1_eager_same_sub (b3, not_guaranteed, Gelem per s): LW 8 N 32 580 and 503 against 513 and 471 (1.13x, 1.07x), N 64 679, 571, 492 against 515, 436, 348 (1.32x, 1.31x, 1.41x), N 128 724, 620, 502, 450 against 506, 413, 354, 281 (1.43x, 1.50x, 1.42x, 1.60x); LW 16 N 32 381 and 383 against 310 and 337 (1.23x, 1.14x), N 64 448, 448, 401 against 333, 337, 280 (1.33x to 1.43x), N 128 523, 523, 451, 385 against 363, 336, 285, 240 (1.44x, 1.56x, 1.58x, 1.61x). The card's sub-warp must-beat (LW 8 N 128 k 64 282) is passed at 450 (1.60x).

Latency per call (one row): LW 8 N 32 848 and 873 against 980 and 1103 (1.16x, 1.26x), N 64 1151, 1144, 1327 against 1953, 2015, 2434 (1.70x to 1.83x), N 128 1867, 1822, 2009, 2078 against 3879, 4522, 5274, 5243 (2.08x to 2.63x); LW 16 N 32 944 against 766 (0.81x), N 64 1098 to 1127 against 1589 to 1746 (1.45x to 1.55x), N 128 1506 to 1755 against 3186 to 4182 (2.11x to 2.47x). At sub-warp the single-row split is a latency win as well from N 64 on.
Against the two-row form (N5_rows_fs_sub, same session) the split is 10 to 20 points lower in throughput at every cell and 1.2x to 1.4x faster in latency per call (one row against two).
negative: LW 16 N 32 (one tile of 16 per set) gains 1.14x to 1.23x only and loses 19 percent in latency: the merge and the recovery are not amortized over one tile.
surprises: The latency gain at sub-warp (up to 2.6x at LW 8 N 128) is larger than the throughput gain (1.6x): the control's sub-warp network is dependency bound on short in-register and shuffle stages, half of which the SIMD word removes, while the throughput regime is pipe bound and pays the recovery's half-rate instructions (T47).

prefer_smaller_index and not_guaranteed share the common path but compile to different kernels in the fast form (the exact ballot fallback is compiled in for prefer_smaller_index, the capped prefix for not_guaranteed), and the prefer_smaller_index kernel carries 3 to 16 more registers and runs 2 to 4 percent slower in throughput in most cells (up to 9 percent at LW 8 N 128), a T28 schedule and register effect of code that never executes on random input. The exact form compiles the same code for both requirements and measured identical throughput to 0.1 percent.
open_questions: Whether the select exchange form would gain the 5 percent it gains on the two-row sub-warp kernel here as well (the split kernels use the ternary form, N5_split_fs_sub exists and was not measured).
